title: Calibration signal card — candidate Sage Wang
content:
Quick context: informal calibration note after loop for Sage Wang (applied for Senior Runtime Engineer). Intended for internal passback / calibration — rough, unpolished. Date of loop: 2025-08-22. Interviewers: Arman G (serving runtime), Priya N (infra), Mei L (product pairing). This is my gut + a compact scorecard to help panel and hiring committee prep.

ONE-LINE SIGNAL
- Leaning towards 'strong maybe' (6/10). Has solid systems instincts and practical debugging chops; needs closer verification on quantization/FP16 depth and at-scale performance reasoning.

SUMMARY NOTES (raw, to self)
- Personality/communication: clear, pragmatic, pauses to check assumptions. Good at translating tradeoffs for PMs. Not overly pedantic.
- Coding: completed a short paired problem (simplified caching logic) with clean tests. Chose clarity over micro-optimizations; used simple modular functions. Occasional off-by-one in buffer indexing but corrected after hint.
- Systems/design: strongest area. Good mental model for request routing, KV cache semantics, and impact of batching on tail latency. Suggested an elegant (but slightly hand-wavy) strategy for cache invalidation when models roll out (versioned keys + epoch tags) — pragmatic and product-aware.
- Inference-specific depth: reasonable familiarity with batching and KV cache, understands effect of sequence length distribution on throughput. Struggled when pressed on low-level quantization tradeoffs (INT8 vs FP16 mixed precision and dynamic range concerns). Couldn't cite specific papers or kernels but had an intuitive take.
- Operability: thoughtful on fallbacks and graceful degradation (canary model variants, region failover). Emphasized metrics to guard regressions (p99 latency + hallucination-rate proxies).

DETAILED SIGNALS
- Problem solving (8/10): fast to decompose, good checkpoints, recovers from mistakes.
- Systems design (7/10): solid architecture thinking, product-aware. Could be stronger on implementation edge-cases.
- Low-level inference expertise (4/10): basic to intermediate; would need coaching on quantization kernels, CUDA/TPU kernel tradeoffs, and memory/prefetch strategies.
- Communication & partnership (8/10): great with product/lang. Would pair well with tech leads and SE teams.
- Culture/operating model fit (7/10): ship-first, pragmatic. Not ideological about every micro-optimization.

RED FLAGS / CONCERNS
- Weak citations: when asked about concrete optimizations (e.g., fused attention kernels, flash attention variants), couldn't name implementations or tradeoffs; relied on generalities. Could be ramped if they have hands-on infra time, but may be slower than a candidate with deep CUDA/ML compiler experience.
- Quantization naivete: didn't confidently explain calibration datasets or dynamic range clipping strategies. Might implement naive INT8 conversion unless mentored.
- Past experience surface: most infra work appears at the application layer rather than kernel-level optimizations. If we need immediate kernel expertise, this is a mismatch.

STRENGTHS / WHY HIRE
- Strong systems architecting instincts relevant to Serving Runtime: routing policies, fallback designs, observability-first approaches.
- Practical debugger: walked through a live p99 spike story and outlined clear triage steps (tracing -> flamegraph -> isolate batch size vs sequence length -> compare model variants).
- Cross-functional communicator: will make SRE/PM/infra alignment easier.

SUGGESTED NEXT STEPS (for team)
- Option A (recommended): bring on for Senior (not Staff) role; pair with an applied-ML/comp-systems mentor focused on quantization and kernel-level optimizations. Run a targeted 1-week pairing project: implement a small batching simulator + evaluate quantization impact (with simple calibration dataset).
- Option B: invite to a focused technical take-home: small repo exercise involving a micro-benchmark (simulate batching + KV cache hits) where candidate must profile and explain latency/cost tradeoffs. This will validate low-level depth quickly.
- Interview follow-ups if proceeding: have someone with deep quantization/CUDA experience (e.g., Lina from applied-ml) ask a kernel-specific follow-up; have SRE do a deeper troubleshooting scenario (complex alert noise + deployment rollback).

HIRE FRAME (comp / level / team)
- Fit level: Senior Engineer (IC3) — not yet Staff/Principal.
- Likely best initial squad: serving-runtime or platform-engineering (routing/observability), not raw kernel/compilation team.

NOTES TO INTERVIEWERS (internal)
- Calibration tip: treat their quantization answers as retrainable skills — focus on validating whether they can read/pattern-match kernel code, tolerate ambiguity, and incorporate feedback.
- If the committee wants a higher bar on low-level inference knowledge, we should either ask for a take-home with profiling or keep searching.

ACTION ITEMS (my todo)
- Share this note with Arman and Priya (done).
- If hiring manager agrees, assign the 1-week pairing validation and confirm comp band.
- Upload kernel follow-up prompt to Linear (INF-2126) and link candidate repo stub.

RAW QUICK QUOTES (as said in loop)
- "I’d prefer versioned cache keys — tag with model epoch so you can invalidate without global drains." (positive: product-aware)
- "For quantization we can probably just use existing toolchains and hope for the best" (concern: underestimates pitfalls).

END — informal note. Use for panel calibration only. Will refine after take-home or pairing.
